# 📊 NBFC Daily Watch — Wednesday, November 18, 2026

Morning edition for Wednesday, 18 November 2026 (IST). Filed late, after the 07:00 run did not fire. Covers Tuesday 17 Nov to early Wednesday. Stock and index figures are Tuesday 17 Nov closes. IBJA's 18 Nov AM session was not posted at writing time, so the IBJA rows are the 17 Nov PM session. AGLOC's 18 Nov block is live.

## 🔴 URGENT / High Impact

### Gold-loan NBFCs ask RBI to review capital and risk-weight rules at Kochi summit
The Federation of Gold Loan Companies (FGLOC) held its first Gold Summit in Kochi on Tuesday 17 November and said it will approach RBI for recognition as a Self-Regulatory Organisation (SRO). The industry has asked RBI to review three things. These are representations, not rule changes: the 12% Tier-I capital requirement for gold-loan NBFCs, against 10% for other lending businesses; the 100% risk weight assigned to gold-loan exposures; and the LTV rules.

George Alexander Muthoot, executive vice-chairman of Muthoot Finance (a listed peer, and a separate company from Muthoot Fincorp), said of the capital ask: "It is not a big ask. The same customer, the same gold and the same currency are involved, whether the loan is given by a bank or an NBFC. Banks have a much larger share of the gold-loan market. There should be a level playing field." He also said more than 75% of the gold-loan sector is represented by FGLOC, and urged smaller lenders to join.

On the SRO plan, Pinaki Nath Banerjee, CEO-designate of FGLOC, said the immediate priority is to expand membership before approaching RBI for SRO status. FGLOC has 23 members, with five more still deciding, and is considering changing the shareholding requirement in its articles so that members can join without taking equity. Banerjee acknowledged an existing SRO for NBFCs: "There is an existing SRO for NBFCs. However, the NBFC sector is extremely large, with approximately 9,075 registered companies."

Banerjee put the organised gold-loan market at ₹19–20 lakh crore: ₹5–6 lakh crore with NBFCs and ₹14–15 lakh crore with banks. RBI data cited by Mint show NBFC loans against jewellery up 69% year on year to ₹3.64 trillion at end-August, and the banks' figure up 83% to ₹5.59 trillion.

The summit also brought warnings on growth and auctions. Mayank Sharma, president-lending at IIFL Finance, said: "At the current gold price, there will be a greater focus on customer collections and interest collections." He expects a significant rise in gold auctions this year once prices stabilise over a longer period, and said: "Consequently, we expect growth to remain muted in Q3," as festive and wedding spending and lower prices pressure borrowers' repayment capacity. Banerjee said repayment challenges have emerged after the correction, though fresh loan demand is healthy, and that growth will continue but not at the same magnitude.

Lenders are moving away from short-term bullet repayments towards monthly or quarterly interest and longer tenures, after RBI's revised gold-loan directions, Economic Times reports.

Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: Muthoot Fincorp is a gold-loan NBFC, so the asks bear on its sector. They are requests to RBI, not rules, so nothing changes for Muthoot Fincorp from this summit. The sources do not say whether Muthoot Fincorp is an FGLOC member.
Sources: [Mint (Subhana Shaikh, 17 Nov)](https://www.livemint.com/industry/banking/gold-loan-nbfcs-seek-rbi-relief-on-capital-norms-as-new-rules-raise-npa-concerns-11794919898824.html) · [ET (Shilpy Sinha, updated 18 Nov 01:58 IST)](https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/banking/finance/banking/gold-loan-nbfcs-seek-lower-capital-requirements-and-risk-weights-call-for-level-playing-field-with-banks/articleshow/135939995.cms) · [BusinessLine (V Sajeev Kumar, 17 Nov)](https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/money-and-banking/fgloc-to-seek-rbi-recognition-as-sro-for-gold-loan-nbfcs/article71711421.ece) · [PTI via The Week (17 Nov)](https://www.theweek.in/wire-updates/business/2026/11/17/gold-loan-industry-braces-for-slower-growth-higher-auctions-amid-gold-price-correction.html)

## 📈 Market & Stock Summary

Indian shares rose on Tuesday. The Nifty 50 closed at 25,387.40 (+0.38%), Nifty Bank at 62,273.25 (+1.13%) and Nifty Financial Services at 28,195.00 (+0.64%). The Sensex closed at 82,532.19, up 427.40 points (+0.52%). Foreign investors were net buyers of ₹4,195.38 crore and domestic institutions of ₹196.93 crore (both provisional). Among the listed peers, Muthoot Finance fell 1.01% to ₹2,749.00, Manappuram 2.37% to ₹296.60 and IIFL Finance 2.45% to ₹636.40. Shriram Finance rose 0.45% to ₹982.85, Bajaj Finance 1.00% to ₹1,121.10, and Muthoot Microfin, a group company, 3.48% to ₹168.92.
Sources: [NSE index closes, 17 Nov](https://nsearchives.nseindia.com/content/indices/ind_close_all_17112026.csv) · [NSE bhavcopy, 17 Nov](https://nsearchives.nseindia.com/products/content/sec_bhavdata_full_17112026.csv) · [Moneycontrol FII/DII data](https://www.moneycontrol.com/markets/fii-dii-data/) · [BusinessLine: Sensex, 17 Nov](https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/markets/sensex-nifty50-today-stock-market-live-updates-17th-november-2026/article71708442.ece)

### Update: Spot gold near $3,850 on Tuesday, down 0.35%
Spot gold was $3,849.59 an ounce at 4:30 p.m. ET on Tuesday 17 November, down 0.35% on the day, according to USA Today. globalgoldprices described the close as its lowest finish since late September 2025. AGLOC's 85% LTV ceiling for 18 Nov is ₹10,448 a gram, ₹60 below the 17 Nov figure (see Gold and LTV below).

Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: a lower gold price lowers the per-gram value of pledged collateral, so loans written close to an LTV ceiling have a thinner cushion. AGLOC's ceilings for 18 Nov are lower in all three LTV bands.
Sources: [USA Today: gold price, 17 Nov 2026](https://www.usatoday.com/story/money/investing/2026/11/17/gold-price-on-november-17-2026/92823314007/) · [globalgoldprices: 17 Nov](https://www.globalgoldprices.com/news/gold-performance-17-november-2026) · [AGLOC](https://www.agloc.org/)

## 🏢 Muthoot Fincorp in the market

### Standing facts (original dates; not new today)

These are carried with their own dates. None is new today.

- Q2 FY27 results (Reg 52), filed 14 Nov 2026: PAT ₹779.41 crore for July–September. Half-year PAT ₹1,485 crore on total income of ₹6,567 crore (PTI). Stage III 1.07% (vs 1.41%). CRAR 19.38%.
- CCCPS conversion: recommended to shareholders on 14 Nov 2026. No meeting date announced.
- IPO: up to ₹3,000 crore fresh issue, at the draft red herring prospectus (DRHP) stage.
Sources: [BSE: Muthoot Fincorp Q2 FY27 filing, 14 Nov](https://www.bseindia.com/xml-data/corpfiling/AttachLive/1b013a70-8ca6-4aff-ae25-9ef12e008024.pdf)

Muthoot Fincorp's investor page, fetched at 07:42 IST today, carried no document dated after 14 Nov 2026. The announcements list is partly loaded by script, so this reads as no new filing seen, not as confirmation that nothing was filed.
Sources: [Muthoot Fincorp investor page](https://www.muthootfincorp.com/investors)

The dated items below are not Muthoot Fincorp filings. Muthoot Microfin's board meets on Thursday 19 Nov on audited half-year accounts that feed Muthoot Fincorp's restated consolidated statements. SEBI's Credit Risk-o-Meter goes live on 21 Nov. RBI's monetary policy committee meets on 2–4 Dec 2026.

## 🏛️ RBI & Regulatory — Headlines Only

RBI's press releases on 17 Nov were routine liquidity and retail items: the result of the two-day VRRR auction held that day, a VRRR to be conducted on 18 Nov, and the SGB 2020-21 Series VIII premature redemption price due 18 Nov. None changes an NBFC rule. Details are in the rules report.
Sources: [RBI press releases](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_PressReleaseDisplay.aspx)

### RBI's Tata Sons letter: Upper Layer listing applies, no exemption
Economic Times reports that RBI's letter dated 16 Nov, addressed to Tata Sons' chief financial officer, says Tata Sons must comply with the rules for Upper Layer NBFCs, "including the requirement of listing by your company". The letter answers Tata Sons' request for guidance. The 17 Nov edition carried the same letter from CNBC-TV18; this is a second report of it, not a new event.

Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: none stated in the sources checked. The letter is addressed to Tata Sons.
Sources: [ET: RBI tells Tata Sons to comply with listing requirement](https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/company/corporate-trends/rbi-tells-tata-sons-to-comply-with-listing-requirement-says-no-exemption-from-upper-layer-nbfc-norms/articleshow/135894889.cms)

# 📋 NBFC Regulatory Daily Report
**Date:** Wednesday, 18 November 2026 (IST)

Morning edition for Wednesday, 18 November 2026 (IST). Filed late, after the 07:00 run did not fire. Covers Tuesday 17 Nov to early Wednesday.

---

## 🔔 New Regulatory Updates Today

No new RBI, SEBI or IBBI instrument on 17 Nov changes a rule that applies to Muthoot Fincorp. What was checked is listed below. A representation to RBI is not a rule change, and the items under "Other 17 Nov items" are not instruments.

What was checked between 17 Nov and early 18 Nov: the RBI notifications feed, where the latest instrument is still the 11 Nov Domestic Money Transfer Directions (RBI/DPSS/2026-27/476); the RBI press releases of 17 Nov, all routine liquidity and retail items (the result of the two-day VRRR auction held that day, a VRRR to be conducted on 18 Nov, and the SGB 2020-21 Series VIII premature redemption price due 18 Nov); SEBI's circular list, which carries one instrument dated 17 Nov on the margin framework for the commodity derivatives segment, not NBFC lending ([SEBI circular](https://www.sebi.gov.in/legal/circulars/nov-2026/review-of-margin-framework-for-commodity-derivatives-segment_105799.html)); and IBBI, where no new instrument for NBFCs appeared.
Sources: [RBI press releases](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_PressReleaseDisplay.aspx) · [SEBI circular, 17 Nov](https://www.sebi.gov.in/legal/circulars/nov-2026/review-of-margin-framework-for-commodity-derivatives-segment_105799.html)

### Other 17 Nov items (reported, not rule changes)

- RBI letter to Tata Sons: RBI's letter dated 16 Nov, addressed to Tata Sons' CFO, says Tata Sons must comply with the rules for Upper Layer NBFCs, "including the requirement of listing by your company". It answers Tata Sons' 6 October request for guidance. It is a reply to one company, not a new instrument, and the 17 Nov edition already carried the CNBC-TV18 report of it.
Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: none stated in the sources checked. Muthoot Fincorp's layer is not given in them.
Sources: [ET: RBI tells Tata Sons to comply with listing requirement](https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/company/corporate-trends/rbi-tells-tata-sons-to-comply-with-listing-requirement-says-no-exemption-from-upper-layer-nbfc-norms/articleshow/135894889.cms)

- FGLOC gold-loan asks: the Federation of Gold Loan Companies asked RBI, at its Kochi summit on 17 Nov, to review the 12% Tier-I capital requirement, the 100% risk weight on gold-loan exposures and the LTV rules. They are representations, and they do not change any rule. No RBI response is reported in the sources checked.
Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: none on any rule today. Muthoot Fincorp is a gold-loan NBFC, so the asks bear on its sector if RBI later takes them up.
Sources: [Mint (17 Nov)](https://www.livemint.com/industry/banking/gold-loan-nbfcs-seek-rbi-relief-on-capital-norms-as-new-rules-raise-npa-concerns-11794919898824.html) · [ET (18 Nov)](https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/banking/finance/banking/gold-loan-nbfcs-seek-lower-capital-requirements-and-risk-weights-call-for-level-playing-field-with-banks/articleshow/135939995.cms)

The 16 Nov RBI registration actions (Press Release 2026-2027/1500 and /1501) and SEBI PR No.73/2026 were covered in the 17 Nov report and are still in the latest-circulars list below. They are not repeated as today's news.

cards.summary: The Federation of Gold Loan Companies (FGLOC) held its first Gold Summit in Kochi on Tuesday 17 November and said it will approach RBI for recognition as a Self-Regulatory Organisation (SRO). The industry has asked RBI to review three things.
cards.impact: Muthoot Fincorp is a gold-loan NBFC, so the asks bear on its sector. They are requests to RBI, not rules, so nothing changes for Muthoot Fincorp from this summit. The sources do not say whether Muthoot Fincorp is an FGLOC member.
